title: Establish SLO bands and weighted model fallback + deployment safety nets for regional burst scenarios
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a set of SLO bands (gold/silver/bronze and burst) for interactive chat and embeddings traffic that include precise latency targets, availability thresholds, and per-period error budgets. Design a weighted model fallback strategy that routes traffic to alternate model variants and regions based on configurable weights, and specify deployment safety nets (canary thresholds, automated throttles, circuit-breaker triggers) to protect error budgets during regional burst events. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, trade-offs, and handoffs for engineering and SRE work.
acceptance_criteria: SLO bands defined with clear numeric targets: gold p95 <= 120ms, silver p95 <= 250ms, bronze p95 <= 600ms, burst best-effort with p95 <= 1s
Availability targets specified per band: gold 99.95% monthly, silver 99.9%, bronze 99.5%
Error budget windows and burn-rate rules documented for each band (daily and 30-day windows), with automated gating actions when burn-rate > 3x for 1 hour
Weighted fallback policy documented and API-ready: weight tables for model variant selection by origin region, with deterministic tie-breaking and version compatibility constraints
Rollout gates include: canary at 1% traffic for 30 minutes, health checks on p50/p95/error-rate, automated rollback at canary failure conditions
Circuit-breaker policy that reduces inbound traffic by 20/50/80% when regional error budget depleted for respective bands
Telemetry dashboards and alerts live in Console: per-tenant SLO burn-rate, p95 by model variant and region, fallback router metrics, and canary health timeline
Runbook and escalation path created and reviewed by SRE and Support; links included in ticket
E2E test plan and a simple simulation harness exist that can reproduce regional burst and fallback routing in staging
tasks: Finalize numeric SLOs with data from perf benchmarks and customer tiers
Design and document weighted fallback decision tree and configuration format
Implement rollout gating hooks in deployment pipeline and Console UI for canary parameters
Add metrics (p50/p95/p99, errors, fallback-rate, weight-applied) to per-route telemetry
Create and validate automated throttle/circuit-breaker logic in routing layer
Author runbook and acceptance playbook; schedule walkthrough with SRE and Support
Build staging simulation harness and execute predetermined burst scenarios
Coordinate on release notes and customer communications for new SLO bands
decisions: Use banded SLOs (gold/silver/bronze) rather than per-tenant custom SLOs initially to reduce complexity; per-tenant SLOs will be evaluated in a follow-up project
Weighted model fallback chosen over strict priority routing to allow gradual degradation and to distribute load across compatible variants; weights default to model quality-preserving fallbacks
Circuit-breaker percentages are conservative (20/50/80) to avoid oscillation; SRE can tune in real-time via feature flags
Canary duration set to 30 minutes to capture cold-start and traffic pattern variance, with auto-rollback thresholds defined on p95 and error-rate rather than p50

implementation_notes: Plan to implement fallback as a pluggable router policy: 1) Evaluate model compatibility and latency cost, 2) Apply configurable weight table to produce distribution across candidates, 3) Emit deterministic routing events for audit and debugging. Canary and circuit-breaker hooks will be implemented in the deployment orchestrator; feature flags will control rollout. Telemetry will tag requests with original model, selected fallback, and weight_applied. Simulation harness will replay real traffic traces with injected regional latency/error profiles to validate SLO gating and throttle behavior.
